Question Choices: Select. What can be concluded about opposite sides of a parallelogram? ~~No relationship is guaranteed | They are congruent | They must have different measures~~
Hints: A diagonal creates two congruent triangles.|Use CPCTC on the opposite side pairs.
Solution: Opposite sides are parallel by the definition of parallelogram. A diagonal creates two congruent triangles by alternate interior angles and their shared side (ASA); corresponding opposite sides are therefore congruent.

Question Choices: Select. What do the diagonals of a parallelogram do to each other? ~~They bisect each other | They are always perpendicular | They always have equal lengths~~
Hints: Their intersection is the midpoint of each diagonal.|Each diagonal is split into two congruent segments.
Solution: A parallelogram has half-turn symmetry about its diagonal intersection. The half-turn exchanges the endpoints of each diagonal, so the intersection is the midpoint of both. Thus the diagonals bisect each other. A rhombus is also a parallelogram.

Question Choices: Select. What can be concluded about opposite angles of a parallelogram? ~~They are congruent | They must have different measures | No relationship is guaranteed~~
Hints: A diagonal creates congruent triangles.|Use corresponding angles after proving triangle congruence.
Solution: Opposite sides are parallel. Each of two opposite angles is supplementary to the same adjacent angle, so they have equal measures and are congruent.

Question Choices: Select. A diagonal divides a parallelogram into two triangles. Are the triangles congruent? ~~Yes | No~~
Hints: Opposite sides are parallel.|Use alternate interior angles and the shared diagonal.
Solution: Yes. In parallelogram ABCD, draw AC. Since AB is parallel to CD and BC to AD, alternate interior angles give angle BAC = DCA and angle BCA = DAC. The included side AC is shared. Therefore triangles ABC and CDA are congruent by ASA.

Question Choices: A parallelogram diagonal has length 18 and is bisected by the other diagonal. Find the length of each half.
Hints: Bisect means divide into two equal parts.|Compute 18/2.
Solution: The diagonals bisect each other, so the two pieces of the 18-unit diagonal are equal. Each half measures 18/2 = 9.

Question Choices: Select. In a rhombus how do the diagonals intersect? ~~At right angles | At 30-degree angles | At 60-degree angles~~
Hints: A rhombus has four congruent sides.|Its diagonals form right angles.
Solution: The diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular. The diagonal intersection bisects each diagonal; two adjacent small triangles have equal rhombus sides, a shared half-diagonal and equal halves of the other diagonal. SSS makes their adjacent intersection angles equal; since these sum to 180 degrees, each is 90 degrees.

Solution: A parallelogram has half-turn symmetry about its diagonal intersection. The half-turn exchanges the endpoints of each diagonal, so the intersection is the midpoint of both. Thus the diagonals bisect each other. A rhombus is also a parallelogram.

Question Choices: Find the area of a rhombus with diagonal lengths 10 and 16.
Hints: Use one half the product of the diagonals.|Compute (10 times 16)/2.
Solution: The perpendicular diagonals divide the rhombus into four right triangles. Their areas total half the product of the full diagonals: A = 10 × 16 / 2 = 80 square units.

Question Choices: A rhombus has area 54 and one diagonal has length 9. Find the other diagonal length.
Solution: Use A = d1 × d2 / 2: 54 = 9d/2. Multiply by 2: 108 = 9d. Divide by 9: d = 12. Check: 9 × 12 / 2 = 54.

Question Choices: Adjacent angles of a parallelogram measure (3x) degrees and (2x) degrees. Find x.
Solution: Adjacent parallelogram angles are supplementary: 3x + 2x = 180. Thus 5x = 180 and x = 36. The angles are 108 and 72 degrees, which sum to 180.
